title: KNLiveDbg Windows defense-evasion research and claim ledger

scope.platform: Windows x64 kernel, process, file-system, telemetry, and security-product impairment
scope.interpretation: Systematic public-source coverage of the listed technique families; it is not a claim that private or unpublished research is enumerable.
exclusions: claims inferred only from an adjacent telemetry source

sources.title: Bind Link Abuse: One Windows Feature, Many Ways to Blind Your EDR
sources.version_note: Research article and linked author tooling describe File-Binding, Process-Binding, and Silo-Binding.
sources.primitive: bindflt mappings can decouple visible paths from the file object and image backing used for execution

sources.title: The Immutable Illusion: Pwning Your Kernel with Cloud Files
sources.version_note: Author research documents Cloud Filter-backed False File Immutability and Redux/GodFault-Redux.
sources.primitive: CloudFiles state changes can violate executable file immutability after a trust decision

sources.title: EDR killers explained: Beyond the drivers
sources.version_note: Telemetry-backed study of almost 90 EDR killers and driverless impairment techniques.
sources.primitive: security products are terminated, suspended, disconnected, or impaired through reusable driver and driverless primitives

sources.title: T1685 Throttle Cybersecurity Agent Network Traffic via QoS Policy
sources.version_note: Living upstream test reviewed at the QoS policy atomic GUID 7dd05b3e-0803-4852-9345-c494eb3e40fe.
sources.primitive: an ActiveStore per-application QoS rule can throttle a security agent to eight bits per second

sources.title: Shedding light on the ABYSSWORKER driver
sources.version_note: Reverse engineering enumerates callback removal, dispatch replacement, minifilter detach, and thread/process termination handlers.
sources.primitive: a kernel driver can remove callbacks, replace dispatch tables, detach filter devices, and terminate security threads

sources.title: Process Injection Using Windows Thread Pools
sources.version_note: Black Hat Europe 2023 research page describing eight PoolParty variants.
sources.primitive: worker-factory, task, completion, and timer queue objects can retain dormant cross-process execution callbacks

sources.title: Update on Windows Downdate
sources.version_note: Follow-on to the Black Hat USA 2024 and DEF CON 32 Windows Downdate research.
sources.primitive: trusted Windows update flows can roll back CI, kernel, secure-kernel, and hypervisor components while normal version posture appears current

sources.title: Detection Strategy DET0577 for KernelCallbackTable hijacking
sources.version_note: Version 1.0; page last modified 2026-05-12.
sources.primitive: unexpected PEB KernelCallbackTable modification followed by GUI callback execution

sources.title: Detection Strategy DET0467 for TLS callback injection
sources.version_note: Version 1.0; page last modified 2026-05-12.
sources.primitive: PE TLS-directory modification and hollowing can redirect execution before the nominal entry point

sources.title: Finding vulnerable drivers with hooking and reading result verification
sources.version_note: Open-access BYOVD Detector paper, volume 9 article 166.
sources.primitive: dispatch discovery plus symbolic reachability and read-result verification can identify unknown vulnerable IOCTL paths with fewer false positives

sources.title: Unveiling BYOVD Threats: Malware's Use and Abuse of Kernel Drivers
sources.version_note: NDSS 2026 paper DOI 10.14722/ndss.2026.231491; authors report a virtualization-based end-to-end kernel trace over 8,779 malware samples and 773 signed drivers.
sources.primitive: correlating the originating user request with dispatch, indirect kernel control flow, and resulting sensitive actions exposes previously unknown BYOVD behavior

sources.title: PsLookupProcessByProcessId function
sources.version_note: WDK contract documents referenced EPROCESS return semantics and STATUS_INVALID_CID for absent client IDs on Windows Vista and later.
sources.primitive: a candidate process ID can be independently converted to a referenced EPROCESS or rejected as an invalid client ID

sources.title: PsLookupThreadByThreadId function
sources.version_note: WDK contract documents referenced ETHREAD return semantics and STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER when a thread ID is absent.
sources.primitive: a thread client ID can be resolved to a referenced ETHREAD, providing an exported comparison surface for direct CID-entry decoding

sources.title: Volatility 3 Windows handle-table traversal
sources.version_note: Pinned develop commit fffd844b8ed7df500e74115a0ee6f818e6afa59f; the current parser masks the low three TableCode bits and recursively walks 4 KiB pointer or entry arrays.
sources.primitive: handle-table levels and allocated pointer pages provide an independent structural bound instead of trusting only a scalar high-water field

sources.title: ReactOS executive handle-table implementation
sources.version_note: Pinned master commit c606fd79b1c879bad37e49a69e71986dfbc2052e; the implementation documents level 0/1/2 lookup, tag-bit clearing, and NextHandleNeedingPool as the allocated-range bound.
sources.primitive: a valid handle-table allocation grows through contiguous low-level pages whose capacity and lookup bound must agree

sources.title: RX-INT: A Kernel Engine for Real-Time Detection and Analysis of In-Memory Threats
sources.version_note: arXiv v1.
sources.primitive: event-driven thread creation plus stateful VAD and memory hashing reduces TOCTOU gaps for manual maps and module stomping

sources.title: An In-kernel Forensics Engine for Investigating Evasive Attacks
sources.version_note: arXiv v2 reviewed.
sources.primitive: low-artifact longitudinal kernel provenance provides process, thread, IRP, and Fast-I/O evidence before attackers clean up

sources.title: Trace of the Times: Rootkit Detection through Temporal Anomalies in Kernel Activity
sources.version_note: arXiv v1.

techniques.title: Security callback removal with owner persistence
techniques.observable: A stable callback identity disappears in the same boot while current callback/module coverage is complete and the owning image remains loaded.

negative_controls.contains: callback removal comparison skipped because current

techniques.title: Same-identity EPROCESS protection change or evidence removal
techniques.observable: The exact EPROCESS protection byte changes for a stable same-boot process identity, or its protection record disappears while the process remains.

negative_controls.contains: process protection removal comparison skipped because current process-security coverage is incomplete

techniques.title: Whole-security-process suspend or freeze
techniques.observable: Every thread of a known security process has resolved nonzero SuspendCount or FreezeCount in two stable fresh scans with complete inventory.

detector_anchors.contains: L"thread suspend/freeze state coverage is incomplete"

negative_controls.contains: all-thread suspend/freeze evidence was not stable across fresh scans

limitations: A live fixture must not suspend a real security product; only non-destructive host observation and isolated synthetic controls are permitted.
techniques.next_action: Add an isolated expendable process fixture for whole-process suspension semantics without targeting an installed security product.

techniques.title: WFP security-product communication blocking
techniques.observable: An enabled WFP block or bitmask-block filter contains a decoded application identity targeting a known security product or anti-cheat process.

techniques.title: Known BYOVD and EDR-killer artifact correlation
techniques.observable: Loaded drivers, driver services, process images, hashes, and security-product impairment behavior match a curated published artifact or profile.

techniques.title: Policy-based QoS throttling of security agents
techniques.observable: A Policy-based QoS rule with an extreme throttle targets a known security-product executable and exposes complete policy-store metadata.
limitations: The detector covers Policy-based QoS state; independent traffic shaping outside the NetQos policy surfaces remains a separate technique.
techniques.next_action: Add a separately attributable control for non-NetQos traffic shaping before extending the detector claim.

techniques.title: Global Bind Filter File-Binding and Process-Binding
techniques.observable: An active global mapping crosses a protected/security boundary or an exact visible process source disagrees with two agreeing kernel-backed image identities.
limitations: Silo-scoped mapping enumeration and in-silo file identity remain unsupported.
techniques.next_action: Design silo Job discovery and in-silo mapping enumeration without inferring either from the host-global view.

techniques.title: CloudFiles False File Immutability current-state provenance
techniques.observable: A SEC_IMAGE backing is a CloudFiles placeholder and correlates with PP/PPL state, modified data, or an independent deep live-versus-disk mismatch.
limitations: Current state does not reconstruct dehydrate/rehydrate callbacks or immutable file-generation history.
techniques.next_action: Add file-generation provenance only when an independent read-only observable becomes available.

techniques.title: Filter Manager attachment detach or disappearance
techniques.observable: A documented Filter Manager instance becomes detached or disappears in the same boot while the volume and independently registered filter persist and coverage is complete.

negative_controls.contains: minifilter attachment removal comparison skipped because current attachment or callback coverage is incomplete

limitations: The documented Filter Manager view does not prove arbitrary legacy device-stack topology or causal attribution.
techniques.next_action: Retain arbitrary legacy device-stack topology as a separate unsupported technique until an independent bounded inventory exists.

techniques.title: Manual map, module stomping, and transient executable-memory provenance
techniques.observable: Executable VAD/page state, loader and backing-file cross-views, thread/APC/stack provenance, and live-versus-disk bytes disagree.

detector_anchors.contains: thread suspend/freeze state coverage is incomplete

limitations: Periodic collection leaves a TOCTOU gap compared with event-driven stateful hashing.
Headerless kernel executable pages are not yet covered by a full ownership sweep.
techniques.next_action: Add event-driven or higher-frequency provenance capture and a header-independent executable-page ownership corpus.

techniques.title: Full PspCidTable process and thread cross-view
techniques.observable: Stable typed process or thread objects decoded directly from every allocated PspCidTable entry disagree with ActiveProcessLinks, both EPROCESS/KPROCESS thread lists, SystemProcessInformation, Toolhelp, or the exported lookup views for the same live PID/TID, object address, owner, create time, and lifecycle.

detector_anchors.contains: NextHandleNeedingPool disagrees with the independently walked allocated-leaf capacity

limitations: The dual-function RIP-relative anchor is fail-closed when public code layout or validated handle-table metadata is ambiguous.
The live sweep is a bounded multi-snapshot comparison rather than an atomic kernel snapshot; coherent create/exit transitions are suppressed and partial or identity-changing views fail coverage.
Direct object typing depends on matching public PDB geometry and current x64 object-header encoding; unsupported builds fail closed instead of using fixed offsets.
techniques.next_action: Add an offline mutation corpus for restored CID and thread-list unlink combinations without modifying the live host.

techniques.title: Dormant Windows thread-pool object graph injection
techniques.observable: Worker-factory start routines, TP task/timer queues, IOCP completion keys, and ALPC/job/wait callbacks point to unowned executable memory before execution.
limitations: Current VAD/thread/APC/stack evidence generally observes these variants only after execution.
techniques.next_action: Build a read-only worker-factory and thread-pool object graph collector with benign thread-pool negative controls.

techniques.title: Unknown signed-driver sensitive IOCTL reachability
techniques.observable: A user-reachable IOCTL path controls or returns sensitive MSR, CR, I/O-port, physical-memory, or privileged kernel API state.
limitations: The current BYOVD catalog is artifact- and metadata-driven and cannot characterize a previously unknown driver's IOCTL semantics.
techniques.next_action: Add an offline analyzer interface and labeled public-driver corpus before integrating any semantic risk claim.

techniques.title: Windows component rollback and downgrade attestation
techniques.observable: Booted CI, kernel, secure-kernel, hypervisor, and VBS component versions or measurements fall below an independently trusted installed policy baseline.
limitations: Current CI/VBS state reports configuration but does not attest component version history against an external baseline.
techniques.next_action: Design an offline signed-component baseline and boot-measurement comparison that cannot trust the inspected installation alone.

techniques.title: KernelCallbackTable ownership invariant
techniques.observable: A GUI process PEB callback entry changes or points outside the expected executable module ownership and correlates with write or message execution.
limitations: Generic VAD and write provenance do not enumerate or baseline the KernelCallbackTable itself.
techniques.next_action: Add a per-process PEB callback-table snapshot with module ownership and same-identity temporal controls.

techniques.title: TLS callback directory ownership invariant
techniques.observable: A loaded image TLS directory or callback array changes after load, points outside expected executable ownership, or precedes anomalous thread execution.
limitations: Generic PE/VAD integrity does not retain a dedicated TLS callback baseline.
techniques.next_action: Add bounded TLS-directory parsing and same-image baseline controls with ordinary static TLS as negatives.

techniques.title: Transient kernel hook timing anomaly
techniques.observable: Repeated controlled kernel function measurements exhibit a statistically significant timing-distribution shift.
limitations: Current periodic static reads do not collect calibrated function timing distributions.
techniques.next_action: Keep as a research prototype until hardware, load, power-state, and virtualization false-positive controls are available.

techniques.title: Trusted EDR response control-plane abuse
techniques.observable: An authenticated response action lacks valid operator, policy, tenant, and approval provenance despite executing through the trusted EDR.
limitations: Local kernel memory cannot establish remote control-plane authorization or operator intent.
techniques.next_action: Require product-side control-plane audit logs and authorization evidence outside KNLiveDbg's local-memory scope.
